arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:?set BACKUP_DEST to the backup destination (host:path or local mount)}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*) scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/" ;;
    *)   cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/" ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command: sh -n backup.sh && rm -rf /tmp/backup-test && mkdir -p /tmp/backup-test/logs /tmp/backup-test/dest && printf 'line\n' > /tmp/backup-test/logs/app.log && cd /tmp/backup-test && BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/backup-test/dest sh /tmp/backup-test/../backup.sh 2>/dev/null || true

tmp=$(mktemp -d) && cp backup.sh "$tmp/backup.sh" && mkdir -p "$tmp/logs" "$tmp/dest" && printf 'test log\n' > "$tmp/logs/app.log" && (cd "$tmp" && BACKUP_DEST="$tmp/dest" sh backup.sh) && test -f "$tmp/dest/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" && echo TEST_OK && rm -rf "$tmp"

Finished `backup.sh`.

It now:
- reads the backup destination from the `BACKUP_DEST` environment variable and fails fast if it is missing
- creates `logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz` from `logs/`
- copies the tarball to a local mount path with `cp`, or to a remote `host:path` with `scp`
- reports success only after the copy completes

I also validated it with `sh -n` and a local end-to-end test.

Note: `BACKUP_DEST` must be set in the cron environment for tonight’s run.
